1.w: Do not rebuke an older [man], but exhort [him] as a father; younger [men] as brothers;

2.w: older [women] as mothers; younger [women] as sisters, in all purity.

4.w: But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn to be devout first to [their] own household and to give back recompense to parents, for this is acceptable before God.

5.w: Now she who [is] truly a widow and having been left alone has hoped on God and continues in supplications and prayers night and day.

6.w: But she given to luxury has died [while] living.

7.w: Also command these things, so that they may be above reproach.

8.w: But if anyone does not provide for [his] own, and especially [his] household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

9.w: Let a widow be enrolled, being not less than sixty years [old], the wife of one man,

10.w: being testified to in good works: if she brought up children, if she entertained strangers, if she washed the feet of the saints, if she gave relief [to] [those] being oppressed, if she followed after every good work.

11.w: But refuse younger widows; for when they might grow wanton against Christ, they want to marry,

12.w: having judgment because they set aside the first faith.

13.w: And at the same time also they learn [to be] idle, going around the houses, and not only idle but also gossips and busybodies, speaking things not being proper.

14.w: Therefore I intend [for] younger ones to marry, to bear children, to manage their households, to give the one opposing no occasion in favor of reviling.

15.w: For already some turned aside after Satan.

16.w: If any believing [woman] has widows, let her give relief to them, and let the church not be burdened, so that it may give relief to those truly widows.

17.w: Let the elders presiding well be counted worthy of double honor, especially those laboring in the word and the teaching.

18.w: For the Scripture says, “You shall not muzzle an ox treading out grain,” and, “The worker [is] worthy of his wages.”

19.w: Do not receive an accusation against an elder, except upon two or three witnesses.

20.w: But those sinning, rebuke before all, so that the rest may have fear also.

21.w: I earnestly testify before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels that you should keep these things without prejudice, doing nothing according to partiality.

22.w: Lay hands on no one quickly, nor share in the sins of others; keep yourself pure.

23.w: No longer drink water, but use a little wine, because of the stomach and your frequent ailments.

24.w: The sins of some men are evident, going before [them] to judgment; but some also they follow after.

25.w: Likewise also, the good works [are] evident, and even those being otherwise [are] not able to be hidden.
